subject: MAP + Evaluation: Precision benchmarking plan for embeddings + reranker (timeline & deliverables)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP + Evaluation: Precision benchmarking plan for embeddings + reranker (timeline & deliverables)

Samira —

Thanks for the productive call yesterday. Per our MAP items, attaching a concise performance plan you can review. High level ask: we want to validate the embeddings -> reranker pipeline under AtlasSearch production-ish load and agree go/no-go criteria for production traffic. Key metrics we will measure:

- Latency: p50 / p95 / p99 for each endpoint (embedding encode, reranker request-to-response)
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) on reranker streaming responses
- Throughput: end-to-end QPS and tokens/s for the reranker stage
- Concurrency behavior: tail latency as concurrency increases (1, 4, 8, 16, 32 concurrent sessions)
- Cold vs warm cache: warm KV cache runs to show steady-state, plus cold-start run for comparison

Planned dataset & traffic profile (attached perf-run-0308.jsonl):
- 25k query samples (mix: 60% short queries, 30% mid, 10% long), sampled from AtlasSearch prod sample set
- Reranker input sizes: top-50 pre-ranked docs per query
- Payload sizes and embedding dimensions match your reported schema (see atlas_map_v3.xlsx)

Target SLOs (proposal):
- Embeddings endpoint: p95 <= 60ms, p99 <= 120ms at baseline concurrency 8
- Reranker endpoint: TTFT <= 150ms p50, response p95 <= 400ms at concurrency 8 (batched)
- End-to-end throughput: sustain 120 QPS steady state with p95 latency within SLOs

Execution plan & responsibilities:
- Redwood executes the bench runs in our dedicated cluster using the load script (reranker-loadscript.jmx) and collects Prometheus/Grafana metrics. Monica will own run execution and artifacts.
- AtlasSearch provides a short allowlist for test IPs and an integration key for a sandboxed test model endpoint OR we can run against your staging cluster if you prefer.
- Deliverables: raw metrics (CSV/JSON), latency histograms, perf run summary, and a short slide with recommendations (quantization, batching settings).

Timeline (proposed):
- 2027-03-17: final MAP sign-off + access granted
- 2027-03-18 - 2027-03-19: bench runs (warm and cold profiles)
- 2027-03-22: delivery of results + recommended tuning + quick sync to review

Please confirm the access model (Redwood-run vs Atlas-run) and whether the dataset in atlas_map_v3.xlsx requires any anonymization before we run. If you’re good, we’ll lock the run window and Monica will schedule the test run.

Thanks —
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
viv ek.kulkarni@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0193

Vivek —

Thanks, this looks comprehensive and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifications before sign-off:

1) Access: We prefer Redwood to run the benchmark against our staging cluster (we'll give IP allowlist and short-lived API key).
2) Dataset: The sample contains customer IDs; we need a brief anonymization step. I can scrub IDs and re-share by EOD today.
3) SLOs: Your proposed reranker p95 400ms looks reasonable — can you also include p99 tail numbers for concurrency 16/32 in the final report? Our compliance team will ask.

If you can confirm those two items (we'll handle anonymization; you run tests), we can sign the MAP and open the staging key on Thursday morning.

—Samira

Samira — thanks for the quick reply and the preference. Confirming:

- Redwood will run the bench against your staging cluster using the provided key (monitored, short-lived).
- We will not persist any customer IDs; if you still prefer to scrub, that’s fine — just let us know when the scrubbed file is uploaded to the Drive link.
- We’ll include p99 for high-concurrency (16, 32) in the detailed report and highlight any amplification in tail latency.

Monica & Aditya — can you own the Thursday morning run if Atlas opens the staging key by 09:00 PT on 2027-03-18? Please plan for:
- Baseline run (concurrency 1, 4, 8) warm cache
- Scale sweep (8, 16, 32) with p99 collection
- Cold-start test: restart model server and run a 1x pass
- Artifacts: latency histograms (per-endpoint), consolidated CSV, and a 1-page exec summary.

Samira — we'll also post run playbook + k6/ JMeter scripts to the shared Drive link. If anything changes on your side, flag it here and we’ll adjust.

Best —
Vivek

Vivek / Samira —

I can own the run Thursday morning (confirmed). Quick execution details so Atlas knows what to expect:

- Test harness: JMeter (reranker-loadscript.jmx) for traffic orchestration, with Prometheus scrape + Grafana dashboards. We’ll also capture application-level logs for TTFT measurement.
- Run cadence: 30-minute steady-state windows for each concurrency level (1, 4, 8, 16, 32). Three passes per window (to reduce noise).
- Warm/cold: warm = run 3 short priming passes; cold = reload model process and run single pass
- Metrics we will produce: p50/p90/p95/p99, throughput QPS, tokens/s, CPU/GPU utilization, network egress, and TTFT distribution for streaming responses.
- Acceptance criteria for MAP close: end-to-end p95 within proposed SLOs OR documented mitigation plan with expected improvement and timeline (e.g., quantize model to int8, change batching window).

Artifacts to deliver within 48 hours after completion:
- Raw CSV/JSON metrics (per-run)
- Latency histograms and percentile table
- Summary slide (1 page) with go/no-go recommendation and three suggested tuning levers with expected impact estimates

Samira — if you could please share the staging key + IP allowlist before 08:30 PT on 2027-03-18 and confirm whether we should run with the scrubbed dataset (preferred) or if you want us to anonymize on upload.

Aditya / Neha — I’ll pair with you during the run for live monitoring and quick mitigation if we see instabilities.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
